Lore / Peoples Of The Shattered Sea

Peoples of the Shattered Sea

The Shattered Sea sits at the edge of the colonial world. West of the Galewall is the known: kingdoms, records, recognized law. East of it is the Scatter, and the Scatter does not ask where you came from.

The further east you travel, the less the colonial map means. The Crown Islands look like the western homelands transplanted to warmer water. Kalowe and the Midchain look like what happens when those homelands stop being able to enforce anything. The Tail and the Outer Reach look like what was here before the homelands arrived.

This is not a census. The sea moves people too quickly for counts to hold.

Presence Terms

TermMeaning
DominantThe majority of any given town or crew.
CommonReliably present. You will see them every day. No one comments on it.
PresentVisible in any large port. You might go a week without one in a small settlement.
RareOccasional. Noticed. Not remarkable enough to cause trouble.
IsolatedA specific community exists. Everywhere else: almost never.

The Crown Islands

Dravosi colonial core. The western homelands with a tropical accent.

The Crown Islands are the oldest colonial foothold in the Scatter. The majority population is human and came with the Dravosi flag. Rattkin are present in every Crown port even though the Dravosi Crown’s relationship with The Passage is adversarial. The Warren prefers it that way.

The Central Strait

The main highway. The most transient, and therefore the most everything.

The Strait is not a place people live — it is a place people pass through. Port Tidefall processes hundreds of ships a year. Calveno turns over its dockside population on the tide. Calveno specifically skews more diverse than the rest of the Crown Islands — the Tessarine Concordat does not care about your heritage. It cares about your credit.

The Midchain

Free ports and local councils. The colonial map stops meaning much here.

The Midchain has been occupied by too many different peoples for too long for any one of them to claim it. The free ports and reef-knowledge economy select for people who can work outside recognized law. Humans remain common but are not dominant.

The Verdant Teeth

Grung territory. The beach is as far as outsiders go.

The Verdant Teeth interior belongs to the Grung Clans. The coastline operates a strict beach-trade system: outsiders come to the waterline, goods change hands, outsiders leave. The clans do not negotiate on this.

SpeciesPresenceNotes
[[grungGrung]]Dominant
Visiting tradersPresentAt designated beaches only. No overnight presence.
[[tabaxiTabaxi]]Rare

The Tail

Fishing communities and salvage crews at the edge of the charts.

The Tail does not have colonial administration. It has pilot families. What this produces is a working meritocracy defined by capability rather than heritage. The Maw’s proximity draws the Sentinels of the Eyrie and anyone with elemental affinity who has felt the Maw’s pull and cannot stay away.

SpeciesPresenceNotes
HumanCommonLongline crews, salvage camp labour, staging island residents.
OrcCommonPhysical work in hard conditions.
TortleCommonLong-lived, cold-resistant, comfortable at depth. Ideal salvage crew.
GoliathCommonCliff-work, heavy salvage, cold-water diving. Tail communities have had Goliath pilot families for generations.
Sea ElfPresentHalythion contact. Surface occasionally near the Shelfworks approaches.
[[aarakocraAarakocra]]Present

Air GenasiPresentNavigation in fog and bad weather.

HalflingRareProvisioning. The staging islands need someone to run the stores.
[[rattkinRattkin]]Rare

The Sunken Crown and Outer Reach

Past the Maw. The oldest maps and the newest ignorance.

The Sunken Crown is Tabaxi territory. The Keth-Naar community has been here longer than any colonial record acknowledges. They do not seek outside contact; they manage it when it arrives. Beyond the Blue Hole, the Outer Reach belongs to whatever was here before anyone started naming things.

SpeciesPresenceNotes
[[tabaxiTabaxi]]Dominant
Sea ElfRareHalythion trade contact. Respectful, careful, usually carrying specific purpose.
TritonRareDeep-water beyond the Blue Hole.
Water GenasiRareDrawn to the Blue Hole’s elemental behaviour.
Other outsidersRareMaw-crossers, pilgrims, salvagers, the lost. Keth-Naar has protocols for all of them.

On the Water

Ships are their own demographic. A working crew in the Scatter does not look like any port’s population — it looks like whoever the captain could hire and keep.

A Midchain free-trade crew might be half orc and tortle with a rattkin pilot and a grung surgeon who does not discuss what caste they left. A Crown naval vessel runs formally human with dwarf engineers and a rattkin aboard in an unofficial capacity everyone pretends not to notice. A Passage runner has no species requirement and one rule.

The ship is the smallest unit of real integration in the Scatter. It works because it has to.
